text.p: These are the leading stories in Albania's main newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An editorial urges President Sali Berisha to resign, saying he can not guarantee peace, calm and security in Albania.

- Self-styled king Leka Zogu and his royal court minister Abedin Mulosamni turned down a request from prosecutors to give explanations about an illegal demonstration of armed monarchy supporters in Tirana where one person was killed and another five injured.
- Socialist Party and its leftist allies will have 107 out of 155 seats in the new parliament while the ousted Democratic Party only 28.
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told his Albanian counterpart Bashkim Fino Italy will continue to help Albania to overcome the deep economic crisis and rebuild democratic institutions.
- Albania needs a president for all Albanians, out of any political party, Rexhep Mejdani, Socialist Party secretary-general and possible candidate for president, says in interview.
- Democratic Party warns Socialists not to adopt a new constitution, saying the parliament resulting from June 29 elections is not legitimate.
- The ethnic Greek Human Rights Union Party is likely to take part in the coalition government headed by Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano.
- Four people were killed in Vlore on Thursday following a gunfight between rival gangs trying to control the port town.
- Hands off white uniforms, the Health Ministry said in an appeal adressed to gunmen terrorising hospitals and medical staff across the country.

- An editorial bitterly attacks authorities in Macedonia over their violence against ethnic Albanians, saying they should not forget that more than seven million Albanians living in Albania, Macedonia and Kosove would never tolerate discrimination against their ethnic kin.
- The Alba multinational protection force will start leaving Albania on July 18 with Greek, Romanian and Italian troops departing first.

- Greek and Albanian border police met to discuss a recent incident in Sopik village where Greek workers entered some 800 metres inside the Albanian border. They assured the Albanian side such incidents would never happen in the future.
- Social Democratic Party leader Skender Gjinushi will be the next speaker of parliament while his deputy Paskal Milo will be named foreign minister.
- Vigilante groups in Berat have terrorised the town, forcing residents to flee for fear of retaliation.
